title: India and Uzbekistan Seal Long-Term Uranium Deal as Modi Elevates Ties
excerpt: PM Modi secures a long-term uranium supply arrangement with Uzbekistan and upgrades the bilateral relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
body:
• India and Uzbekistan agreed to establish a long-term uranium supply arrangement during PM Modi's visit to Tashkent, securing a diversified fuel source for India's expanding civilian nuclear power program.
  • The two nations upgraded their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, the highest tier of India's bilateral frameworks, marking 15 years of strategic ties.
  • A new Foreign Ministers-level Coordination Council will oversee bilateral cooperation, while the Joint Commission has been elevated to ministerial level.
  • Bilateral trade has crossed $1 billion and both countries are targeting $5 billion by 2030, with defence co-production, AI, and critical minerals on the agenda.

India locked in one of its most significant nuclear energy agreements in years on Sunday, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi announcing a long-term uranium supply arrangement with Uzbekistan — one of the world's top producers of the fuel that powers civilian reactors.

The announcement came during delegation-level talks between Modi and Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace in Tashkent, as the two countries also upgraded their bilateral relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

A Strategic Fuel Source for India's Nuclear Ambitions

India is in the midst of a major nuclear energy expansion, with several new reactors planned under its long-term power strategy. Securing a diversified, long-term uranium supply chain reduces dependence on any single supplier and strengthens India's energy security, according to Outlook Business.

Uzbekistan, a landlocked Central Asian republic, ranks among the world's top uranium producers. The long-term supply arrangement gives India a stable pipeline of nuclear fuel as it scales up reactor capacity to meet growing electricity demand and its climate commitments.

"On this special occasion, we have decided to elevate our relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. We will move forward by setting concrete goals within this new framework."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi

New Institutional Architecture

Beyond the uranium deal, Modi and Mirziyoyev agreed to a series of institutional upgrades that signal a structural deepening of ties. A Coordination Council at the Foreign Ministers' level will be established to oversee all aspects of bilateral cooperation. The existing Joint Commission, previously operating at the secretary level, has been elevated to ministerial level — giving senior political leadership direct oversight of cooperation across trade, energy, and diplomacy, according to Nation Press.

Three sister-city and sister-state arrangements were also formalized during the talks. Modi drew a parallel between Uzbekistan's "New Tashkent" mega-project and India's GIFT City in Gujarat, inviting an Uzbek delegation to study best practices and development models used in the financial hub.

Trade, Defence, and Beyond

Bilateral trade between India and Uzbekistan has crossed $1 billion, according to Modi, who said the two countries are now targeting $5 billion by 2030. To reach that goal, both sides will work on improving market access, banking and payment systems, and connectivity. A joint business summit bringing together leaders from both countries' private sectors will also be organized.

Defence cooperation will form another pillar of the upgraded partnership. The two nations plan to expand co-production and co-development between their defence industries, while also deepening collaboration on digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and space technology.

Both countries reaffirmed a zero-tolerance policy toward terrorism, extremism, and separatism, which Modi described as major challenges to regional stability.

Uzbekistan Confers Highest State Honour on Modi

The visit carried additional diplomatic symbolism when Mirziyoyev conferred Uzbekistan's highest state honour — the Order of "Oliy Darajali Dustlik" — on Modi, the 36th international honour received by the prime minister. Modi dedicated the distinction to the friendship between the two countries and the 1.4 billion people of India.

The Tashkent visit is part of India's broader Connect Central Asia policy, which seeks to build stronger political, economic, and energy linkages with the region. With institutional mechanisms now upgraded and energy, trade, and city-level cooperation on the table, the next phase will test whether these frameworks translate into measurable outcomes on the ground.
